title: Ex 3.4 #15 · Four officers from a club of 15
prompt: A club has 15 members. In how many ways can it fill the offices of president, vice-president, secretary and treasurer, if no one holds more than one office?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4, 10!/7! or binom(10, 3). P(n, k) and C(n, k) work too.

mistakes.hint: The four offices are different jobs, so it matters who gets which one: order matters here.
One person can't hold two offices, so the number of candidates drops after each choice.

hints: Fill the offices one at a time, starting with president.
Each office you fill leaves one fewer person for the next.
solution: There are 15 choices for president, then 14 for vice-president, 13 for secretary and 12 for treasurer.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses permutations P(n, k) (Section 3.4).
